Dedicated /web-design-<city>-or/ pages are a strong local-SEO play, but each must be >60% unique copy with real local specifics -- see docs/SEO-PLAYBOOK.md section 2. pricing.$comment: From the approved funnel blueprint. Terms that touch billing start date, hard costs and the guarantee are still open -- see docs/BUILD-NOTES.md and the NEEDS_REVIEW callouts on /terms/.

servicePages.$comment: SEO-PLAYBOOK.md section 1: one dedicated page per service someone would actually search for individually, at /services/<slug>/. Deliberately a subset of the 8-item list above -- lead capture, analytics, and ongoing support don't have real standalone search intent, so they're mentioned inside these pages ('what's included') rather than getting three thin pages of their own. None of these sell standalone: every page funnels to the $799 Willamette 30-Day Program, since that's the only real price that exists.

forms.$comment: The free presence check form is the funnel's soft-conversion path. It is wired to Netlify Forms: Netlify detects the form in the deployed HTML and captures POSTs to '/', so there is no backend to run. It only works on a Netlify deploy — locally the POST fails and site.js shows the phone-number fallback, which is correct behaviour, not a bug.
forms._todo: Netlify does NOT email you by default. After the first deploy open Netlify > Forms > presence-check > Settings > Form notifications and add an email notification to info@willametteweb.com, then submit a real test and confirm it arrives. Until that is done the submissions are captured but nobody is told, which looks exactly like a working form and loses every lead. Set this flag to true once a test email has actually landed.
